newsitem.title: CHINA: Income gap widens in Shanghai in 1996 first half.
newsitem.headline: Income gap widens in Shanghai in 1996 first half.

text.p: The gap between the rich and poor in Shanghai widened in the first half of 1996, official media reported on Sunday.

A survey of 500 residents found that the richest in Shanghai earned 1,268.93 yuan a month in the period, against 300.14 yuan earned by the poorest, a gap of 968.79 yuan, against a gap of 857.73 yuan in the same 1995 period, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper on Sunday reported the city's Statistical Bureau as saying.
It did not say how many people were included in the rich and poor categories.

The average monthly income of Shanghai residents in the period was 643.75 yuan, a nominal increase of 15.6 percent over the same 1995 period and an inflation-adjusted increase of 4.2 percent, it said.

The bureau said that food accounted for 50.1 percent of the spending of Shanghai people in the period, down from 53.9 percent in the same 1995 period, clothing 9.7 percent, down from 10.5 percent, transport and communications 8.4 percent, up from 4.6 percent, and entertainment and education 9.7 percent, up from eight percent.
The newspaper gave no further details.
